dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule: arm-specific intervention schedules and interventions descriptions: "Ixekizumab" "Blinded Treatment Period: 160 milligrams (mg) ixekizumab given subcutaneously (SC) at baseline followed by 80 mg ixekizumab every 2 weeks (Q2W) SC from week 2 to week 10." "At week 12, 80 mg ixekizumab and placebo given SC." "Open Label Period: 80 mg ixekizumab given SC every 4 weeks (Q4W) with an option for Q2W dosing starting at week 24, week 28 or week 40." "Placebo" "Blinded Treatment Period: Placebo given SC at baseline followed by placebo given SC Q2W from week 2 to week 10." "At week 12, 160 mg ixekizumab given SC." "Open Label Period: 80 mg ixekizumab given SC Q4W with an option for Q2W dosing starting at week 24, week 28 or week 40." "Ixekizumab" "Administered SC" "Placebo" "Administered SC" -- The CT.gov intervention descriptions are retained verbatim. The two arm descriptions document distinct schedules: the Ixekizumab arm receives 160 mg ixekizumab at baseline, 80 mg every 2 weeks in Weeks 2-10, 80 mg ixekizumab plus placebo at Week 12, then 80 mg every 4 weeks in the open-label period with an option for every-2-week dosing starting at Weeks 24, 28, or 40; the Placebo arm receives placebo at baseline and every 2 weeks in Weeks 2-10, 160 mg ixekizumab at Week 12, then the open-label ixekizumab schedule. The schema's dosing_periods can represent only unqualified time intervals and cannot encode these arm-specific dose/frequency changes, so the collection is left empty rather than implying the same schedule for both interventions; frequency, duration, and units_per_dose remain null. The latest protocol amendment's detailed schedule was considered separately for response-driven escalation under timing_ops.rescue_therapy.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: 5.1 Inclusion Criteria, criteria 3-5: "[3] Have an overall sPGA ≥3 at screening (Visit 1) and at baseline (Week 0," "Visit 2)" "[4] Have sPGA of Genitalia ≥3 at screening (Visit 1) and at baseline (Week 0," "Visit 2)" "[5] Have BSA involvement of ≥1% at screening (Visit1) and at baseline (Week 0," "Visit 2)" -- All three thresholds are required at screening and baseline (Week 0, Visit 2). The protocol permits a lower BSA subgroup but its entry threshold remains at least 1%.

prohibited_concomitant: Biologic agents other than investigational product
Natalizumab or other agents targeting alpha-4 integrin
Topical corticosteroids more potent than mild during Study Periods 1 and 2
permitted_concomitant: Bath oils and oatmeal bath preparations, subject to visit timing restrictions
NSAIDs, aspirin, or acetaminophen/paracetamol as needed
value.population_note: The protocol lists permitted and prohibited concomitant therapies rather than a standardized assigned background regimen. Some topical products are allowed only outside specified genital-area, treatment-period, or visit-timing restrictions.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 6.8 Concomitant Therapy, Table RHBQ.6.2; protocol identifier: "are or are not permitted for use during the study and related comments and conditions for use." "Concomitant Medication Permitted/Not Permitted in Study Periods 1, 2, and 3" "Biologic agent other than Not permitted Minimum required time since last biologic agent dose" "Natalizumab, or other agents Not permitted  Must have never received" "Systemic nonbiologic psoriasis Not permitted  Must not have received within 4 weeks prior to" "Phototherapy Not permitted  Must not have received within 4 weeks prior to" " Study Periods 1 and 2: Not permitted for use" "Vaccines, live Not permitted  Must not have received within 12 weeks prior to" "Bath oils and oatmeal bath Permitted with conditions  Not to be used within 12 hours prior to a study" "NSAIDs, aspirin, or Permitted  Allowed as needed" "acetaminophen/paracetamol" -- The registry and protocol describe active drug versus placebo; they do not establish monotherapy or a standardized background regimen. multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 6.4 Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity: "A multiple testing strategy for the primary and the major secondary endpoint will be" "implemented to control the family-wise Type I error rate at a 2-sided α level of 0.05." "primary and major secondary endpoints will be sequentially tested in the following order to" "compare ixekizumab Q2W versus placebo, using the primary analysis method specified in" "Primary – Proportion of patients achieving sPGA of Genitalia (0,1) at Week 12" "Major Secondary #1 – Proportion of patients achieving an overall sPGA (0,1) at" "Week 12" "Major Secondary #2 – Proportion of patients with at least a 3 point improvement in" "genital psoriasis itch Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) within the GPSS at Week 12." "will be calculated for patients who had baseline score of at least 3." "Major Secondary #3 – Proportion of patients achieving a SFQ Item #2 score of 0 or 1," "at Week 12." "This will be calculated for patients who had baseline score of at least 2." "The primary endpoint will be tested at 2-sided α = 0.05." "If the test for primary endpoint is" "significant, then the test for the major secondary endpoint #1 will be performed." "major secondary endpoint #1 is significant, then the test for major secondary endpoint #2 will be" "performed." "If a test is not significant, all subsequent tests will be considered not significant." "There will be no adjustment for multiple comparisons for any other analyses." "4." -- A fixed sequential gate tests the primary then three major secondary endpoints at the 2-sided 0.05 level, stopping inferential significance when a test fails; this controls error for that family only. Other analyses are explicitly unadjusted. No statement explicitly establishes SAP finalization.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: 4.1 Overview of Study Design; Appendix 2 Schedule of Activities: " Period 1: Screening Period (Visit 1 and Visit 1A) will assess patient eligibility and start" "e-diary data collection, occurring approximately 7 to 30 days prior to Period 2 (baseline;" "Week 0; Visit 2)." " Period 2: Blinded Treatment Period will occur from Week 0 (Visit 2) up to Week 12" "(Visit 7)." "Two injections of ixekizumab 80 mg SC (total dose of 160 mg) or 2 injections of placebo" "SC, respectively, will be given at Week 0 (Visit 2)." "From Week 2 through Week 10" "patients will receive ixekizumab 80 mg Q2W SC or placebo Q2W SC (Section 6.1)." " Period 3: Open-Label Treatment Period will occur from Week 12 (Visit 7) up to" "Week 52 (Visit 12)." "During the remainder of Period 3, patients will receive ixekizumab" "80 mg Q4W dosing with an option to step-up to Q2W dosing starting at Week 24 through" "Week 40 (at Visit 9 [Week 24], Visit 10 [Week 28], or Visit 11 [Week 40]) (Section 6.1)." " Period 4: Post-Treatment Follow-Up (Visit 801 through Visit 803) is for safety" "This period occurs from the last treatment period visit or" "early termination visit (ETV) up to a minimum of 12 weeks following that visit." "All procedures to be conducted during the study, including timing of all procedures, are indicated" "in the Schedule of Activities (Appendix 2)." "Schedule of Activities" "Schedule of Activities, Protocol I1F-MC-RHBQ" -- Screening is approximately 7–30 days before Week 0. The randomized blinded period is Weeks 0–12; open-label treatment is Weeks 12–52. Follow-up lasts at least 12 weeks from the last treatment visit or ETV, so its absolute study week and total duration vary. The source includes Appendix 2's Schedule of Activities; visit cadence was not reduced to a single interval here.

value.rationale: In Period 3, the patient and investigator may determine that additional ixekizumab is needed to achieve or maintain satisfactory disease control; the protocol permits increasing ixekizumab 80 mg from every 4 weeks to every 2 weeks starting at Week 24, 28, or 40, and maintains the increased frequency through treatment completion or early discontinuation. This response-driven dose escalation is distinct from the scheduled Week 12 transition to open-label ixekizumab.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Protocol I1F-MC-RHBQ(b), Sections 6.1 and 6.6: dose escalation eligibility, timing, and continuation: "Dosing may be increased in the Open-Label Treatment Period" "(Period 3) to ixekizumab 80 mg Q2W, starting at Week 24 through Week 40 (at Visit 9" "[Week 24], Visit 10 [Week 28], or Visit 11 [Week 40]), if the patient is eligible to receive" "additional investigational product (that is, if it is determined by the patient and the investigator" "that the patient needs additional ixekizumab in order to achieve or maintain satisfactory disease" "All patients who increase dosing to 80 mg Q2W will remain on this dose until" "b Dosing may be increased to ixekizumab 80 mg Q2W starting at Week 24 through Week 40 (at Visit 9 [Week 24], Visit 10 [Week 28], or Visit 11 [Week 40])." "regimen to Q2W starting at Week 24 through Week 40 as outlined in Section 6.1." -- Using the latest posted protocol version, Amendment (b), for the final study design. The schema has no dedicated response-driven dose-escalation field; the permitted, discretion-triggered increase in study drug frequency is represented here and distinguished from the scheduled Week 12 crossover.
